items.title: Warren Vaché interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 23, 1995
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Ralph Sutton has an attitude that’s quite like that... [INTERVIEWEE] Well Ralph is in a situation and at a stage in his life where he can say that.

ctx.x: Ralph Sutton has an attitude that’s quite like that, and he seems to say I’m not going to do anything I don’t want to do. And I said, gee, that’s nice.

Well Ralph is in a situation and at a stage in his life where he can say that. Now I’m supporting a fourteen year old and an eight year old, an ex-wife, and myself. So much as I would like to say I’m not going to do anything I don’t want to do, very often the reality is get me something to do, you know?

It’s interesting to go into these jazz parties and cruises and so forth that, like you said, you don’t have much control over who you’re going to play with. And the idea of having a repertory of tunes in your head I think is imposing to students who think about, well I know The Real Book or I know every sixth page of The Real Book or something. But you really have to have a pretty vast songlist in your head I would think, because you get into situations and —
